title: Childcare Workers
description: Attend to children at schools, businesses, private households, and childcare institutions. Perform a variety of tasks, such as dressing, feeding, bathing, and overseeing play.

tasks.text: Care for children in institutional setting, such as group homes, nursery schools, private businesses, or schools for people with disabilities.
Dress children and change diapers.
Provide care for children with physical, developmental, or mental health disabilities.
Regulate children's rest periods.
Instruct children in health and personal habits, such as eating, resting, and toilet habits.
Help children with homework and school work.
Read to children and teach them simple painting, drawing, handicrafts, and songs.
Discipline children and recommend or initiate other measures to control behavior, such as caring for own clothing and picking up toys and books.
Sanitize toys and play equipment.
Sterilize bottles and prepare formulas.
Perform housekeeping duties, such as laundry, cleaning, dish washing, and changing of linens.
Accompany children to and from school, on outings, and to medical appointments.
Maintain a safe play environment.
Organize and store toys and materials to ensure order in activity areas.
Assist in preparing food and serving meals and refreshments to children.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Communicate with children's parents or guardians about daily activities, behaviors, and related issues.
Support children's emotional and social development, encouraging understanding of others and positive self-concepts.
Observe and monitor children's play activities.
Identify signs of emotional or developmental problems in children and bring them to parents' or guardians' attention.

clusters.label: Coordinating the Work and Activities of Others

tasks.text: Perform general personnel functions, such as supervision, training, and scheduling.
Organize and participate in recreational activities and outings, such as games and field trips.
Keep records on individual children, including daily observations and information about activities, meals served, and medications administered.
Perform general administrative tasks, such as taking attendance, editing internal paperwork, and making phone calls.
Create developmentally appropriate lesson plans.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Computer based training software
skills.def: Software to create, manage, or provide instructional material or courses accessed from a computer. Examples: Educational software, Schoology.

skills.name: Multi-media educational software
skills.def: Software to educate children or students using interactive or gaming elements. Examples: Nearpod, Seesaw.

skills.name: Project management software
skills.def: Software to plan, organize, staff, or control the completion of a product or set of tasks. Examples: Google Classroom.

skills.name: Calendar and scheduling software
skills.def: Software to plan or organize the activities of a person or group. Examples: Scheduling software.
